title: A universal loss-limited optimum for fixed multi-pass quantum sensing per absorbed photon
summary: Multi-pass schemes send a photon through a sample several times to learn more about it. When the sample rather than the light is scarce, the natural figure of merit is the information gained per photon the object absorbs. We show that one constant fixes the loss-limited optimum of every fixed scheme in which a single photon passes repeatedly through the sample and is detected once at the end. Three properties suffice: information that grows as the square of the pass number, a fixed survival probability per pass, and no dose from a photon already lost.
